summary: A hotel as Data Fiduciary must keep reasonable security safeguards over guest personal data, including data its processors handle; highest penalty tier.
hotel_trigger: Processes digital personal data of guests or staff in India

summary: The hotel must inform the Data Protection Board and each affected person of a personal data breach in the prescribed form and manner.
hotel_trigger: Personal data breach affecting guests or staff in India

summary: Personal data must be erased when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is served unless law requires it to be kept.
hotel_trigger: Holds guest data after the stay

summary: Notice must come with or before a consent request; consent must be free, specific and informed and as easy to withdraw as to give.
hotel_trigger: Relies on consent for marketing, loyalty or optional data

summary: Processing data of persons under 18 needs verifiable parental consent and no tracking or targeted advertising aimed at children.
hotel_trigger: Family bookings or loyalty profiles that include minors

summary: Requests to access, correct, update or erase data must be answered within 90 days at most.
hotel_trigger: Any guest rights request in India

summary: Each affected person must be told of a breach without delay in plain language with a description, likely consequences, mitigation, safety steps and a contact point.
hotel_trigger: Personal data breach affecting guests in India

summary: The Board must be told of a breach without delay and then within 72 hours of becoming aware (or a longer period the Board allows on written request) with updated detail, mitigation and a report on notices given; the rule applies eighteen months after publication (Rule 1).
hotel_trigger: Personal data breach in India

summary: Reasonable security safeguards must include encryption, masking or tokenisation, access control, logging and monitoring, backups and keeping logs and related personal data for one year unless another law needs longer; the rule applies eighteen months after publication (Rule 1).
hotel_trigger: Processes personal data in India

instrument: CERT-In Directions 2022 under s.70B(6) of the IT Act
provision: Incident reporting and point of contact
summary: Listed cyber incidents must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them and a designated point of contact kept up to date.
hotel_trigger: Any body corporate in India, including every hotel company

instrument: CERT-In Directions 2022 under s.70B(6) of the IT Act
summary: Logs of all ICT systems must be kept for a rolling 180 days within Indian jurisdiction and clocks synchronised to NIC or NPL time sources or ones traceable to them.
hotel_trigger: Any body corporate in India

instrument: Bureau of Immigration Form III (earlier Form C)
summary: Foreign guest particulars must be submitted online within 24 hours of arrival and of departure, kept electronically for at least one year and opened for inspection.
hotel_trigger: Accommodates any foreign national including OCI cardholders

summary: Reported as the current statutory basis for the foreign guest register with penalties; commencement and detail are secondary. Tracking only, not scored.
hotel_trigger: Accommodates foreign nationals

instrument: RBI circular RBI/2022-2023/95 on storage of actual card data
summary: Merchants must not store card on file data; for guest checkout, card data may be kept only until settlement or T+4 days, whichever is earlier.
hotel_trigger: Accepts card payments in India

instrument: RBI Regulation of Payment Aggregators Directions, 2025
summary: Aggregators must check merchant PCI DSS status at onboarding and keep card credentials off merchant servers; the duty reaches the hotel through its aggregator contract.
hotel_trigger: Takes online payments through a payment aggregator

summary: The controller must apply appropriate technical and organisational measures and keep a record of processing.
hotel_trigger: Processes personal data in the UAE outside the DIFC and ADGM

summary: The UAE Data Office must be notified of a breach that prejudices privacy, confidentiality or security. Affected people are told where they are prejudiced. The Law text sets no hour count.
hotel_trigger: Personal data breach at a UAE property

summary: Transfers abroad go only to countries with adequacy approved by the Data Office or under listed cases such as contract terms or explicit consent.
hotel_trigger: Guest data held by providers outside the UAE

instrument: DIFC Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020
summary: Security must be appropriate to the risk and the Commissioner of Data Protection notified as soon as practicable after a breach.
hotel_trigger: Hotel or operator entity established in the DIFC

summary: The Office of Data Protection must be notified without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach.
hotel_trigger: Hotel entity registered in ADGM

summary: Licensed Abu Dhabi hotels must join the smart check in platform, integrate the PMS and protect guest data including facial biometrics, using it only for registration and verification.
hotel_trigger: Licensed hotel establishment in Abu Dhabi

summary: Subscribed Dubai hotels warrant technical security measures, run a yearly security assessment, report actual or suspected incidents immediately and destroy guest data after termination.
hotel_trigger: Dubai hotel subscribed to the contactless check in service

instrument: Dubai Hotel Establishments Information e-Programme (Decree No. 13 of 2011)
summary: Reported by a law firm: Dubai hotels register guests electronically with police and tourism bodies and are fined for disclosing the data. Tracking only, not scored.
hotel_trigger: Licensed hotel in Dubai

summary: The supervisory authority must be notified without undue delay and at the latest within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach; processors tell the controller without undue delay.
hotel_trigger: Processes personal data of guests in the EU or offers services to them

summary: Affected people must be told of a breach likely to result in a high risk to them.
hotel_trigger: Processes personal data of guests in the EU

summary: Article wording read only on a secondary site: technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk. Tracking only, not scored.
hotel_trigger: Processes personal data of guests in the EU

summary: Article wording read only on a secondary site: processors only under a binding written contract with set terms. Tracking only, not scored.
hotel_trigger: Uses PMS, booking engine or other processors for EU guest data

summary: Transfers outside the EEA need an adequacy decision, safeguards such as standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules or a derogation.
hotel_trigger: EU guest data held by providers outside the EEA

summary: CCTV needs a documented purpose per camera, layered signage, short retention, no private areas and access control with logging.
hotel_trigger: CCTV at a property in the EU

summary: Non essential cookies need clear information and consent; marketing email needs prior consent except similar offers to existing customers with an opt out.
hotel_trigger: Hotel website or marketing aimed at EU guests

summary: Foreign guests must sign a registration form on arrival and show a valid identity document; electronic registration is allowed with consent.
hotel_trigger: Property in Germany with foreign guests

summary: Traveller data must be sent to the Ministry platform within 24 hours of reservation, cancellation or start of stay and kept for three years.
hotel_trigger: Property in Spain

summary: Reported by a dated secondary note: guest details sent to the Questura within 24 hours of arrival. Tracking only, not scored.
hotel_trigger: Property in Italy

summary: Cookies on the hotel website and electronic marketing to UK guests are regulated; only headings and the government factsheet were read.
hotel_trigger: Website or marketing aimed at UK guests

instrument: PCI DSS (contractual through acquirers and card brands)
summary: PCI DSS applies even when payment is outsourced: keep a written agreement with each provider, check its status at least yearly and define shared duties.
hotel_trigger: Accepts card payments

provision: Notice to residents and state bodies
summary: Affected New York residents must be told within 30 days of discovery, with notice to the Attorney General, Department of State and State Police.
hotel_trigger: Holds private information of New York residents

summary: Reasonable administrative, technical and physical safeguards are required, including a coordinator, training, vendor contracts, testing and secure disposal.
hotel_trigger: Holds private information of New York residents

summary: Notify the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days where 500 or more Floridians are affected and individuals within 30 days; agents tell the entity within 10 days.
hotel_trigger: Holds personal information of Florida residents

instrument: California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA
summary: Businesses over the thresholds must keep reasonable security, disclose retention per category and honour rights to know, delete, correct and opt out.
hotel_trigger: Hotel business meeting a CCPA threshold with California guests

summary: Reported by a law firm: damages per violation for biometric data handling, limited by a 2024 amendment. Tracking only, not scored.
hotel_trigger: Biometric check in, locks or staff time clocks in Illinois
